findings.evidence: Mathlib defines `GL n R` and `GeneralLinearGroup.scalar` under `[Semiring R]` (`GeneralLinearGroup/Defs.lean:39,55`) and `upperRightHom` under `[Ring R]` (`GeneralLinearGroup/FinTwo.lean:196`); the PR applies `[CommRing R]` uniformly at line 98 through all declarations at lines 106–344.
findings.fix: Split the API into `[Semiring R]`, `[Ring R]`, and `[CommRing R]` sections, proving inverse closure directly from the two-sided matrix inverse instead of `adjugate_fin_two`.
findings.issue: The section-wide `[CommRing R]` is too strong: `GL2Borel`, its entry lemmas, `diag`, `torusHom`, and `ne_top` need only a semiring, while `upperRightHom_mem`, `mk`, `equivProd`, and `mem_iff_exists_mk` need only a ring; only `det_val` and `det_diag` require commutativity.

summary: The non-counting API is still unnecessarily restricted to commutative rings; most declarations naturally work over semirings or arbitrary rings.
